## Changes since `v0.7.2-beta.3`

### Features

- install AI agent hooks on an SSH server from its terminal: agents run on servers as often as locally, but their hooks could only be installed on this computer, so a tab running Claude Code or Codex over SSH showed no working or waiting state and sent no notifications unless the user copied the hooks by hand; an SSH terminal's context menu now opens AI agent integration on this server, which reads each agent's config directory from the server's environment (as its login shell sets it up) or its default, and installs, updates or removes the same hooks and plugin files over the tab's SFTP connection, merged beside the user's settings with the previous file kept as .tterm-bak; Codex's Windows hook, which runs this computer's tTerm, is left out on servers ([643d57b7](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/643d57b7dbdfea0dda025356b3068708ebf7fc40))
- pause SFTP following while the terminal is on another host: after an ssh from the connected server to another one, a shell there that reports its directory moved the drawer to paths that mean something else on the connected server, and reports that named their host were ignored altogether; shell integration now reads the server's own name (uname -n) when it installs, a report naming another host pauses following and the follow button says which host the terminal is on, following resumes once the connected server reports again, and the scripts to paste into ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc or config.fish now name their host ([08ddb0f8](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/08ddb0f8b7c6194dd16fd267aeb0f32f3535fee9))
- restore each terminal tab's content after a restart by default: a tab that comes back empty loses what the user was looking at, which Terminal and iTerm2 keep; the snapshot stays capped at 5000 lines per tab and is saved as plain text on this computer, as the setting says, and saved settings keep their values ([95ce9451](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/95ce9451b73351d5f9a87affbb5c09f68e810f50))
- paste on right click by default on Windows: users coming from PuTTY, Xshell and Windows Terminal expect it there, while macOS and Linux keep the context menu; Shift+right-click still opens the menu, and only new installs get the new default ([d36e464f](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/d36e464f36c624c1bfb8821d8bf4d64bff09ccb9))
- give tabs and search the shortcuts each platform expects, and stop default shortcuts taking shell keys: macOS opens and closes tabs on Cmd+T and Cmd+W, as every Mac terminal does, instead of Ctrl+Shift+T and Cmd+Shift+W; Windows and Linux search on Ctrl+Shift+F, as Windows Terminal does, because Ctrl+F moves the cursor in readline and pages in vim and less; the SFTP drawer moves from Ctrl+T, which transposes characters in readline and opens fzf's file finder, to Ctrl+Shift+E (Cmd+Shift+E on macOS), the file explorer chord of VS Code; the keymap settings warn when Ctrl+T or Ctrl+F is bound. Users who never changed these shortcuts get the new ones on upgrade ([29a1a28a](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/29a1a28aadc0a7d58a41de4446c1bfb2b8ef8adb))

### Fixes

- stop Open in Terminal typing cd into a program or on another host: with command marks off nothing told a shell at its prompt from tail -f or a REPL, so the cd line went to whatever had the terminal, and after an ssh to another host it ran there; a line the shell has not come back from (no directory report since Enter, which tTerm's scripts send at every prompt) now counts as busy, and while the terminal is on another host the drawer says so instead of sending the line ([2181a4ad](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/2181a4ad160ebc9344c48f11cda09be0455fe633))
- keep closing a tab on Cmd+Shift+W on macOS: Cmd+W is Close Window in the default macOS menu, so binding it to closing the tab had the shortcut and the menu competing for the same key; Cmd+T keeps opening tabs, as nothing in that menu uses it ([22962f2c](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/22962f2c2c9edfe408282e8d7039b53a4c88be99))
- leave Ctrl and a letter to the terminal on macOS: a Ctrl chord without a binding of its own fell back to the Cmd binding of the same key, so Ctrl+F opened the search bar instead of moving the cursor forward in readline, and any Cmd+letter shortcut took the control character the shell or editor uses; Ctrl+\[, Ctrl+\] and Ctrl+\\ were already exempt, and Ctrl with a digit, = or - still falls back ([525659ae](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/525659ae2bfc4a51641306c957debc310528d09a))
- put prerelease installs on the beta channel from their first launch: the backend, which a first launch reads its config from, always chose stable, while the frontend chose beta-dev for an alpha, beta, rc or dev version, so a fresh beta install stopped receiving betas; the backend now decides from CARGO_PKG_VERSION the same way ([9a215646](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/9a215646b7761269548b14bd545861b490d45a33))
- start new installs on a Nerd Font, with one default font chain on both sides: a first launch reads its config from the backend, whose default was plain Menlo, Cascadia Code or DejaVu Sans Mono, so starship and powerlevel10k icons drew as boxes, while the frontend kept a different JetBrains Mono Nerd Font chain that only startup font warm-up used; both now put JetBrains Mono Nerd Font before each system font, a backend test fails if the two drift, and the Nerd Font hint in font settings checks the first installed font of the chain rather than the chain's text ([831c6504](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/831c6504dd217364e49d9c5bcbde755405b1018c))

### UI and usability

- stop the built-in highlight coloring "ok": the word appears in most command output, so the success rule lit up green far more often than it marked a success; success, succeeded and passed stay green, and sets the user edited keep their own rules ([cf534103](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/cf534103b6015d0b4cac43a132d01f9e1381b367))
- give the terminal text room on the right and at the bottom by default: new installs had 6 px on the left and none elsewhere, so text ran into the scrollbar and the window's bottom edge; the right now matches the left at 6 px and the bottom has 4 px, and saved settings keep their values ([83d6e541](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/83d6e541a88494d6ec38f3249aaa60afdd61b36f))

### Other changes

- say when finished-command notifications cannot come from local terminals: the setting is on by default, but local shells on macOS and Linux mark where commands start and end only with tTerm's shell integration, which is off by default, so the switch looked on while local tabs never notified; the setting now says what local shells are missing and links to Terminal settings ([37ac8062](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/37ac8062e74f3432b2293646a550a962624ccb2d))
